For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:
https://images.redhat.com/
mitigations: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the criteria for a supported mitigation. Red Hat will update this section as more information becomes available.

To mitigate this issue, avoid configuring the `inets` httpd server's `mod_auth` module with `dets` or `mnesia` authentication backends when using multiple directory blocks that require distinct user or group populations. Alternatively, ensure that all protected directories are intended to share identical user populations, thereby eliminating reliance on namespace isolation. If possible, switch to the `plain` authentication backend, which correctly isolates per-directory users and groups.

To mitigate this issue, ensure that applications utilizing the eldap component are configured to connect only to trusted LDAP servers. Additionally, if possible, configure applications to disable or restrict the processing of LDAP referral URLs from untrusted sources, as the vulnerability requires an application to explicitly pass server-supplied referral strings to eldap for parsing.

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to services utilizing the `inets` HTTP server to trusted clients and networks. Alternatively, deploy a reverse proxy in front of the `inets` HTTP server and configure it to enforce body size limits for incoming requests, preventing oversized chunked bodies from reaching the vulnerable server. If a service restart or reload is required for network configuration changes to take effect, ensure proper service management procedures are followed.
